brief_description: The main objective of the Scheme is to assist needy disabled persons in procuring durable, sophisticated, scientifically manufactured, modern, standard aids and appliances that can promote their physical, social and psychological rehabilitation by reducing the effect of disabilities.
description:
The "Scheme of Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances" or the "ADIP Scheme" was launched on 1st Jan 1981 by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, to assist the disabled persons in procuring suitable, durable, scientifically-manufactured, modern, standard aids and appliances, that can promote their physical, social and psychological rehabilitation by reducing the effects of disabilities and enhance their economic potential. Assistive devices are given to PwDs with the aim to improve their independent functioning and to arrest the extent of disability and occurrence of secondary disability. The Scheme shall also include under its ambit, medical/surgical correction & intervention, which is essential prior to the fitment of aids and appliances. The cost could range from ₹ 500/- for the hearing & speech impaired to ₹ 1,000/- for the visually disabled and ₹ 3,000/- for the Orthopaedically disabled. The Scheme is approved for continuation upto 31st March 2026.
Objective - The main objective of the Scheme is to assist needy disabled persons in procuring durable, sophisticated, scientifically manufactured, modern, standard aids and appliances that can promote their physical, social and psychological rehabilitation, by reducing the effects of disabilities and enhancing their economic potential.
Scope - The Scheme will be implemented through the Implementing Agencies. The Agencies will be provided with financial assistance for the purchase, fabrication, and distribution of such standard aids and appliances that are in conformity with the objective of the Scheme. The Implementing Agencies will take care of/make suitable arrangements for fitting and post-fitting care of the aids and appliances distributed under the ADIP Scheme. The scope of the scheme has been further enlarged to include the use of mass media, exhibitions, workshops, etc. for the exchange of information and promoting awareness and distribution and use of aids/appliances.

eligibility_criteria:
ELIGIBILITY OF IMPLEMENTING AGENCIES
The following agencies are eligible to implement the Scheme on behalf of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan) under the aegis of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, subject to fulfillment of the following terms and conditions:
1. Societies and their branches, if any, were registered separately under the Societies Registration Act, of 1860. 1. Registered Charitable Trusts. 1. Indian Red Cross Societies and other Autonomous Bodies headed by District Collector/Chief Executive Officer/District Development Officer. 1. National/Apex Institutes, CRCs, RCs, DDRCs, National Trust, ALIMCO, functioning under the administrative control of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment/Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 1. National/State Handicapped Development Corporations. 1. Local Bodies – Zilla Parishad, Municipalities, District Autonomous Development Councils and Panchayats, etc. 1. Hospitals registered as separate entities, as recommended by State/UT/Central Govt. 1. Nehru Yuva Kendras. 1. Any other organization as deemed fit by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Govt. of India.
NOTE: Grant-in-aid under the Scheme will not be given for commercial production or supply of aids/appliances.
While approving new implementing agencies, preference would be given to those Agencies: (i) Which employ professional/technical expertise, in the form of professionally qualified staff (from RCI recognized courses) for identification, prescription of the required aids/appliances, fitment and post-fitment care of beneficiaries as well as aids/appliances. (ii) Possess infrastructure in the form of machinery/equipment for fabrication, fitment, and maintenance of aids/appliances to be given to a person with a disability under the ADIP Scheme and which have the capacity to produce aids and assistive devices with ISI standards/ISO certification.
ELIGIBILITY OF THE BENEFICIARIES 1. An Indian citizen of any age. 1. Holding a 40% Disability Certificate (Benchmark disability). 1. Having monthly income from all sources not exceeding Rs.30,000/- per month. 1. In the case of dependents, the income of parents/guardians not exceeding Rs. 30,000/- per month. 1. Not having received assistance during the last 3 years for the same purpose from any source. However, for children below 12 years of age, the minimum time of assistance is one year.
Identification of Beneficiaries
i. Through Camp Activity: Implementing agencies will carry out assessments of beneficiaries in camp mode at district levels.
ii. Through Headquarter Activity: The National Institutes/CRCs/ALIMCO/ DDRCs and other implementing agencies will utilize the grants to extend services to eligible beneficiaries who approach their headquarters or their respective Regional Centres.
iii. Through Common Service Centres (CSCs): The Department will enter into an MOU with the CSCs functioning all over the country at Block, Taluka, and Gram Panchayat levels for registration of beneficiaries who need aids and assistive devices under the ADIP Scheme.
iv. Through Mobile App: In order to facilitate the beneficiaries in getting aids and assistive devices, a Mobile app will be launched by the Department which will enable beneficiaries to either place requests for new assistive devices(new registrations) or repair existing devices (existing users). The requests so received on the app will be compiled in the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
v. Through Management Information System (MIS)/ADIP Web Portal: The portal will facilitate PwDs for an online request for providing aids & assistive devices to the eligible beneficiaries within 6 months from the date of such registration on the Portal.

Q: What is the main purpose of the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” A: The scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” has been introduced to inspire, promote, and provide recognition to artists, students of art institutions, and school children across Gujarat by encouraging participation in fine arts and offering awards and exhibition opportunities to deserving talents.


Q: Who is eligible to participate in the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition”? A: The scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” is open to three categories of participants: individual artists residing in Gujarat, students currently enrolled in recognized art institutions within the state, and school children studying in Classes 1 to 10 in schools located in Gujarat.


Q: What kind of artworks are accepted under the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition”? A: The scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” accepts creative submissions in various fields of fine arts including painting, sculpture, graphic arts, applied arts, and visual arts from eligible participants, allowing a wide range of artistic expression.


Q: How many entries can each participant or institution submit to the competition? A: Under the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition,” each individual artist and each student of an art institution may submit a maximum of two entries, while each school may submit up to 14 entries from students in Classes 1 to 5 and another 14 entries from Classes 6 to 10 through the school’s official process.


Q: What is the total value of the prizes awarded through the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition”? A: The scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” distributes a total of 89 prizes with a combined value of ₹2,47,500, divided among artists, art institution students, and school children as a means of recognizing excellence in artistic creation.


Q: How are the winners selected in the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition”? A: In the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition,” all submitted artworks are assessed and judged by panels comprising field-specific experts who select winners based on artistic merit, originality, and overall quality of the work.


Q: What are the different prize categories under the scheme? A: The scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” provides 23 prizes worth ₹1,74,500 in the artist category, 16 prizes worth ₹48,000 in the art institution student category, and 50 prizes worth ₹25,000 in the school children category.


Q: Is there any additional benefit for winning students of art institutions in the scheme? A: Yes, in addition to prize money, students of art institutions who win under the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” are also eligible to receive a monthly scholarship of ₹1,000 funded from the interest earned on a dedicated corpus fund.


Q: What type of recognition do the winners of the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” receive? A: The winners of the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition” receive cash prizes, certificates of merit, an opportunity to showcase their artworks in a dedicated exhibition, and inclusion in a catalogue featuring the prize-winning entries.


Q: Where is the exhibition of selected artworks organized? A: Under the scheme “State Art Exhibition Competition,” the selected and winning entries are exhibited at the art gallery located in Ravi Shankar Rawal Kala Bhavan, providing public exposure and recognition to the artists.

Q: Due to my current circumstances, I have enrolled in a distance education course where I receive all my study materials by mail. Am I still able to get the student allowance? A: No, scholars pursuing their studies through correspondence are strictly not eligible for this financial assistance.
Q: Both my younger sister and I are applying for the educational support, but we currently share 1 cell phone for all our communication needs. Do we each need to provide distinct contact numbers? A: Yes, each applying scholar is required to furnish a separate mobile number.
Q: The college I am currently attending is completely privately run and does not have any formal recognition from the state or central authorities. Does my institution meet the necessary criteria? A: Unfortunately no, you are only eligible if your educational institute is a Government or Government Recognized Institute.
Q: My parent has been working in the manganese ore mines for the past 8 months. Will I be considered for this financial assistance program? A: Yes, you are eligible if your parent is an Iron Ore, Manganese & Chrome Ore Mines worker with at least 6 months of service.
Q: Our household relies entirely on my father's income from beedi rolling, which fluctuates around ₹9,000/- monthly. Is there a specific earnings cap we need to worry about? A: You are eligible, as the total monthly income of a Beedi worker's family from all sources must not exceed ₹10,000/-.
Q: I was recently awarded an academic merit-based grant from a state government agency for scoring top marks in my class. Am I barred from receiving this specific welfare-based financial aid at the same time? A: You may avail of this welfare-based support even if receiving a merit-based one, provided you do not receive more than 1 scholarship within the same category simultaneously.
Q: After successfully finishing my Bachelor of Arts degree last year, I decided to enroll in a Bachelor of Commerce program this year. Can I get financial help for my 2nd bachelor's degree? A: No, students studying in the same stage of education in a different subject after passing 1 stage are not eligible.
Q: If my mother is employed in a clerical position at a limestone mine and earns a reasonably high salary, does her income level disqualify me from receiving the study allowance? A: No, mine workers doing manual, unskilled, highly skilled, and clerical work have no wage limit restrictions to avail of the benefits.
Q: I do not possess a bank account exclusively in my own name, but I do share a joint savings account where my name is listed as the primary account holder. Is this setup acceptable for receiving the funds? A: Yes, in the case of a joint account, it is perfectly acceptable as long as the 1st name on the account is that of the scholar.
Q: Both my mother and father work from home rolling beedis as contract labourers rather than being direct employees. Are their children allowed to apply for the educational support? A: Children of contract workers and home-based workers are fully eligible to apply for this financial assistance.
Q: Considering that my parent works in the film industry and is paid a 1-time flat fee for projects instead of a monthly wage, what is the maximum amount they can earn? A: A cine worker's remuneration must not exceed ₹8,000/- per month, or it must not exceed ₹1,00,000/- if paid in a lump sum or instalments.
Q: I have already completed my professional training to become a teacher with a Bachelor of Education degree and now want to pursue a law degree. Will my new studies be funded? A: No, students who have completed their educational career in 1 professional line and continue education in a different professional line are not eligible.
Q: I recently received my final grades and was successfully promoted to the next academic class on my very 1st try. Does this academic progress meet the requirements for the educational grant? A: Yes, applicants who have passed their last qualifying examination in the 1st attempt and are promoted to the next class are eligible.
Q: My father currently holds a supervisory role in a dolomite mine and receives a monthly salary of roughly ₹9,000/-. What is the maximum permitted salary for his specific job category? A: For persons employed in supervisory and managerial capacities in mines, the wage limit must not exceed ₹10,000/- per month.

brief_description: The scheme aims to address malnutrition among adolescent girls through nutritional and non-nutritional support. Through this scheme, nutritional support, health services, nutrition education and skilling support are provided to adolescent girls aged 14-18 years in identified areas.
description: The scheme "Scheme for Adolescent Girls" has been launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India, and aims to provide a structured support system for adolescent girls through a life cycle approach. The scheme is implemented under Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 through the concerned States/Union Territories. The scheme covers adolescent girls in the age group of 14-18 years in identified areas, including Aspirational Districts of States and North-Eastern States. The services are delivered through the existing Anganwadi Centres and other linked platforms for reaching the beneficiaries. Objectives: - To improve the nutritional and health status and self-development of girls in the age group of 14-18 years. - To provide the adolescent girl with the required linkage with education, life skills, literacy and numeracy skills through the non-formal stream of education, to stimulate a desire for more social exposure and knowledge, and to help them improve their decision-making capabilities. - To train and equip the adolescent girl to improve/upgrade other life skills. - To promote awareness of health, hygiene, nutrition and family welfare, home management and child care and to take all measures, so as to facilitate their marrying only after attaining the age of 18 years and if possible, even later. - To enable a better understanding of environment-related social issues and their impact on the lives of adolescent girls. - To encourage adolescent girls to initiate various activities so that they may become productive and useful members of society.
benefits: Nutritional Benefits: 1. The applicant receives supplementary nutrition containing 600 calories, 18-20 grams of protein and micronutrients. 1. The supplementary nutrition is provided in the form of Take Home Ration (THR). 1. The benefit is provided for 300 days in a year. 1. The Take Home Ration is prepared with fortified micronutrients as per nutritional standards. 1. Age-specific processed food mixtures are labelled to ensure consumption by the targeted beneficiaries. 1. Last-mile tracking of services is undertaken through Poshan Tracker. Non-Nutrition Benefits: 1. Iron and Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation is provided. 1. Health Check-up and Referral Services are provided. 1. Nutrition & Health Education (NHE) is provided. 1. Promotion of menstrual hygiene among adolescent girls is ensured. 1. Participation of adolescent girls is encouraged through the Peer Educator Programme for addressing adolescent issues and awareness about available services. 1. Skill training is provided to generate livelihood opportunities for adolescent girls trained under the scheme.
eligibility_criteria: 1. The applicant should be an adolescent girl in the age group of 14-18 years. 1. The applicant should be identified by the concerned State Government. 1. The applicant should belong to the covered areas under the scheme, including Aspirational Districts of States, including Assam and North-Eastern States. 1. The applicant should have an Aadhaar number to avail benefits under the scheme.
application_process: - The applicant should approach the nearest Anganwadi Centre (AWC). - The concerned State Government identifies eligible adolescent girls under the scheme. - The identified beneficiary details are collected and submitted by the State to the Ministry. - The applicant’s Aadhaar number is used for availing benefits under the scheme. - After identification and registration, the applicant receives eligible benefits, including Take Home Ration and other services, through the concerned delivery platforms.

faqs:
Q: What is IFA Supplementation?
A: The Iron & Folic Acid (IFA) Supplements is provided to address the iron deficiency anaemia as per the National Nutrition Anaemia Control Programme (NNAPP). AGs will be given information by ANM/AWW on food fortification, dietary diversification and advantages of supplementation by IFA tablets, for combating iron deficiency anaemia.

Q: When is the general health check-up for adolescent girls organized?
A: Health check-up of all AGs is organized at least once in three months on a special day called the "Kishori Diwas" which may be synchronized with Village Health & Nutrition Day (VHND) where focused attention on Adolescent specific Health issues may given when immunization is done in the first half and later special sessions may be organized on various issues for AGs.

Q: What is Kishore Health Card?
A: Kishore Health Card provided to the adolescent girl under this scheme is used to record the information about the weight, height, Body Mass Index (BMI) of AGs along with other services provided under the scheme. These health cards for AGs are maintained at the AWCs.

Q: I am a 12 year old girl living in a rural area. Am I eligible to apply in this scheme?
A: Yes, you are eligible to apply.

Q: Are three adolescent girls from the same family eligible to apply in this scheme?
A: Yes, they are eligible to apply.

Q: How do I know if my district is covered under is scheme?
A: The complete list of district under the geographical coverage of SAG can be found in Annexures I and II of scheme guidelines.

Q: Is there any application fee?
A: No. The entire application process is completely free of cost.

Q: Do I need to visit an AWC to get myself identified?
A: The AWW of your locality should visit your home and gather the details.

Q: Will my AADHAAR Number be made public if I provide the detail to the AWW?
A: No. The information containing Aadhaar number will be obtained with the consent of the beneficiary and will be password protected following the SoP issued by MWCD.

Q: Do I need to submit the original copies of the required documents to apply?
A: No, you only need to submit photocopies of Aadhaar Card and the Proof of Age / DOB (Birth Certificate).

Q: How can one know if the data gathered by the AWW is genuine / authentic?
A: The Supervisor would check and authenticate 20% of the entries in the survey registers.

Q: Where can I find the format of the baseline survey form?
A: The form is available in the annexure of the scheme guidelines..

description:
The scheme "Scheme for Adolescent Girls" has been implemented in Bihar since 2011 through the Anganwadi centers under the Integrated Child Development Project (ICDS). Under this scheme, adolescent girls aged 11 to 14 years who are not attending school receive a monthly take-home ration along with skill development training. It is a centrally sponsored scheme with a funding ratio of 50:50 between the Central and State governments.
The main objective of the scheme is to improve the level of health, nutrition, and education by providing support to adolescent girls so that they can become self-reliant and aware. The objective of this scheme is as follows:-

 - To assist in self-development and empowerment of adolescent girls.
 - To improve their nutrition and health status.
 - To raise awareness about health, hygiene, and nutrition.
 - To reintegrate out-of-school adolescent girls into the formal education system or develop alternative education/skills.
 - To develop their home-based skills and life skills.
 - To provide information and guidance about available public services such as Primary Health Centres, Rural Hospitals/Community Health Centres, Post Offices, Banks, Police Stations, etc.
benefits:
1. Under this scheme, beneficiaries receive a monthly take-home ration (THR) along with skill development training.
2. The following benefits are provided to beneficiaries under both nutritional and non-nutritional items:

 - Nutritional items: Rice, eggs, and soybeans are provided as THR to adolescent girls. Nutritious items are provided for 25 days each month. - Non-nutritional items: These include Iron Folic Acid supplements, comprehensive health check-ups and referral services, health and nutrition education, reintegration of out-of-school adolescent girls into the formal education system or mainstreaming through alternative education/skills development, life skills education, home management training, and counseling/guidance for accessing public services.
eligibility_criteria:
1. The beneficiary should be a resident of Bihar.
 1. The beneficiary should be an adolescent girl aged between 11 and 14 years.
 1. The beneficiary should not be currently attending school.

Apart from this, issues can be registered with the Child Development Project Officer at the project level, the District Program Officer/District Officer at the district level, the Divisional Commissioner at the divisional level, and the Director, ICDS, as well as the Additional Chief Secretary/Principal Secretary/Secretary of the Social Welfare Department at the state level. Complaints can be submitted in writing or communicated over the telephone.

A: The scheme is for adolescent girls aged 11-14 years who reside in Bihar and are not attending school.

Q: What benefits are provided under the scheme?
A: Beneficiaries receive a monthly take-home ration, including rice, eggs, and soybeans, along with skill development training, life skills education, health check-ups, Iron Folic Acid supplements, and counseling.

Q: How is the take-home ration (THR) distributed?
A: The THR, which consists of rice, eggs, and soybeans, is distributed every month for 25 days to ensure adequate nutrition.

Q: What is the objective of the scheme?
A: The scheme aims to empower adolescent girls, improve their health and nutrition, raise awareness about hygiene, reintegrate them into the education system, and provide information about public services.

Q: How does the scheme help out-of-school girls?
A: It reintegrates out-of-school girls into formal education or provides skill-based alternative education to help them become self-reliant.

Q: How can one apply for the scheme?
A: To apply, eligible girls must register at their nearest Anganwadi center.

Q: What is the funding mechanism of the scheme?
A: The scheme is funded on a 50:50 basis between the Central and State governments.

Q: Can girls aged 15 and above benefit from the scheme?
A: No, the scheme is only for adolescent girls aged 11-14 who are not attending school.

A: Once a girl resumes schooling, she is no longer eligible for the scheme.

Q: What is the objective of the "Scheme to Assist for Infrastructural Facilities for Gaushalas & Panjrapole"? A: The scheme aims to support animal welfare organizations like gaushalas and panjrapoles by offering financial assistance for the development and construction of essential infrastructure. Q: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme? A: Any gaushala or panjrapole that is registered under the Public Charity Act and meets the specified land and livestock requirements is eligible to apply for the scheme.

Q: What type of financial assistance is provided under this scheme? A: The scheme provides up to 75% of the total cost or a maximum of ₹4.00 lakh for each infrastructure component such as cattle sheds, compound walls, water facilities, and storage units.

Q: Can an organization apply for multiple infrastructure components at once? A: An organization can apply for different components, but financial assistance will be granted for only one component in a given year.

Q: Is it necessary for the organization to own the land where construction will take place? A: No, the organization may either own the land or have it leased for a minimum of 99 years to qualify for the scheme.

Q: Is the benefit of the scheme available more than once? A: Yes, the organization can reapply for assistance for a different component after a minimum of five years.

Q: What does S.O.R. mean in the construction documentation? A: S.O.R. stands for Schedule of Rates, which refers to the standard government-approved rates used to estimate construction costs.

Q: Is there a maximum land limit for eligibility under the scheme? A: No, there is no maximum land limit, but the organization must have at least 3 acres of land.

Q: Where can the application for this scheme be submitted? A: Applications must be submitted online through the iKhedut (https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/)portal, followed by submission of printed applications with signatures and required documents to the board. Q: Is any official verification required after submitting the online application? A: Yes, the printed application must be signed and stamped by both the local veterinary officer and the nodal officer of the Gujarat Gauseva and Gauchar Vikas Board.

Q: What is the deadline for submitting the physical copy of the application and documents? A: All required documents must be submitted to the board within 30 days from the date of the online application.

description: The scheme “Construction of Approach Road” is a sub scheme under the “West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs”. It was launched on 16th September, 2020, by the Department of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal, shall remain in force up to 5 years. Objective of the "West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs”: The objective of the Scheme is to provide state support in the form of fiscal and non fiscal incentives in order to encourage private sector to set up industrial parks on their own land with quality infrastructure so as to catalyze and promote growth of MSME units in the state, boost employment generation, and lead to technology advancement and improved environmental compliance. Objective of the "Construction of Approach Road" Sub-scheme: Through this incentive, Approach Road (Two-lane Road up to a maximum length of 1.5 km from the nearest major road) catering to the AIP, for which the requirement is justified and approved based on factors including distance of the proposed park from existing major road, shall be set up by the concerned State Government agency free of cost.

faqs:
Q: What is the objective of this scheme? A: The “Construction of Approach Road” under the “SAIP for MSMEs” scheme, facilitates the Private Industrial Park in provision with Approach Road catering to the AIP.
Q: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme? A: Any private sector having minimum 5 acre land under its legal possession (by direct purchase, or on lease from the State Govt) can apply through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered under Companies Act/Societies Registration Act /Partnership Act/LLP can apply for setting up a new Industrial Park on the said land. Also, Owner of any existing/operational privately operated. industrial parks can also apply under SAIP, provided:- a) Park area is expanded up to minimum 5 acre in outlying districts and minimum 2 acre in Kolkata and Howrah. b) The individual units have complied with all the necessary clearances for land conversion, fire licence, environmental issues, building plan etc. Q: What is the minimum size of land for a Park under SAIP? A: Minimum area required for a Park with for heterogeneous activities is 5 acre in any district. However, the scheme shall also be extended to parks dedicated entirely/substantially for Logistics and Warehousing Industry. But such parks shall have to be set up outside the municipal limits and must be developed upon a minimum area of 10 acres. Q: What is the role of SPV? A: SPV will develop the Master Plan/Layout plan of the AIP adhering to the Urban Planning/ Town & Country Planning rules and shall have to obtain the master plan/ layout plan approval from relevant State Government Department with respect to adherence of rules (FAR, Land use, Area Statement, Open Space, Fire Safety, Waste water Management, Water Conservation, Drainage, Sewerage, Solid Waste Disposal, Utility shifting, Power, water, telecommunication, road connectivity and network, etc) including conformation of specification of infrastructure facilities/utilities and quality standard. The SPV shall also be responsible for compliance of other statutory norms (Consent to Establish for the Park based on the activities of the proposed Units envisaged, Mutation, Conversion, Exemption of 14Y of WBLR/ UC Acts, if applicable, etc) as relevant from concerned State Government Departments/Govt. of India/ Authorities. All the compliances/ approvals/ licenses shall have to be obtained before construction of the park. Q: What is SPV? A: SPV or Special Purpose Vehicle, which will procure or is in legal possession of the land for the AIP and will be responsible for designing, development, financing, construction, management, operation and maintenance of the AIP. SPV must be a registered entity under the Companies Act. Q: What does Legal Possession of any land mean? A: The basic requirement of legal possession is completion of Mutation process for the proposed land in f/o the SPV, or, in favour of the proponent individuals. For the latter, the said individuals have to make a Development agreement with the SPV giving it liberty to develop the Park upon their land. Q: What are the basic and common infrastructural facilities to be installed in the AlP? A: Common infrastructural facilities mean anything that will be used commonly by the MSME units in the park. Examples are - Land development, boundary walls, internal roads and street lighting, storm water drainage, sewerage system, STP & WTP (if applicable), water distribution network, electrical main distribution network, telecommunication network, common firefighting infrastructure, solid waste disposal site (if applicable), greenery, guardhouse, gate, and misc. civil structure etc. Q: What is desired manner of land/plot/space allotment to individual units? A: The SPV shall allot the saleable land plot/ space of the ATP to MSMEs through open advertisement in newspapers declaring rates of plot of land/ shed / buildings/ installations. In case applications more than the available plot of land/ shed/ buildings/ installations are received then allotment shall be made through lottery. Q: What is the minimum number of units to be accommodated in an Approved Industrial Park? A: There shall be minimum 5 number of independent MSME Units in Park which will cover 60% of the allottable area of the park. Q: What kind of activities are allowed in an AIP? A: - Minimum 60% of allottable area can have different manufacturing activities including Cold Storage, Poultry, Fisheries, Logistics & Warehousing. - Maximum 5% area can have hostel/housing/guest house. - Minimum 10% as open space, or, as per guideline of Building Rule and Ministry of Environment & Forest, Gol. - Rest areas can be used for common infrastructure and greenery. Q: For how long shall the SPV manage the AIP? A: The SPV shall manage and maintain the AIP for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of completion of construction/installation of the Basic and Essential Common infrastructure Facilities and allotment of minimum 80% of the saleable land to MSMEs without change in shareholding pattern. Q: What is the definition of "Approved Industrial Park"? A: Industrial Park for MSMEs approved by "State Level Empowered Committee" (SLEC) under the Scheme and subsequently notified by the State Government in the Department of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal.

Q: What is the objective of this scheme? A: The “Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities” under the “SAIP for MSMEs” scheme, aims to provide one time back-ended incentive for development of Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities based on land area.
Q: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme? A: Any private sector having minimum 5 acre land under its legal possession (by direct purchase, or on lease from the State Govt) can apply through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered under Companies Act/Societies Registration Act /Partnership Act/LLP can apply for setting up a new Industrial Park on the said land. Also, Owner of any existing/operational privately operated. industrial parks can also apply under SAIP, provided:- a) Park area is expanded up to minimum 5 acre in outlying districts and minimum 2 acre in Kolkata and Howrah. b) The individual units have complied with all the necessary clearances for land conversion, fire licence, environmental issues, building plan etc. Q: What is the minimum size of land for a Park under SAIP? A: Minimum area required for a Park with for heterogeneous activities is 5 acre in any district. However, the scheme shall also be extended to parks dedicated entirely/substantially for Logistics and Warehousing Industry. But such parks shall have to be set up outside the municipal limits and must be developed upon a minimum area of 10 acres.
Q: What is the role of SPV? A: SPV will develop the Master Plan/Layout plan of the AIP adhering to the Urban Planning/ Town & Country Planning rules and shall have to obtain the master plan/ layout plan approval from relevant State Government Department with respect to adherence of rules (FAR, Land use, Area Statement, Open Space, Fire Safety, Waste water Management, Water Conservation, Drainage, Sewerage, Solid Waste Disposal, Utility shifting, Power, water, telecommunication, road connectivity and network, etc) including conformation of specification of infrastructure facilities/utilities and quality standard. The SPV shall also be responsible for compliance of other statutory norms (Consent to Establish for the Park based on the activities of the proposed Units envisaged, Mutation, Conversion, Exemption of 14Y of WBLR/ UC Acts, if applicable, etc) as relevant from concerned State Government Departments/Govt. of India/ Authorities. All the compliances/ approvals/ licenses shall have to be obtained before construction of the park. Q: What does Legal Possession of any land mean? A: The basic requirement of legal possession is completion of Mutation process for the proposed land in f/o the SPV, or, in favour of the proponent individuals. For the latter, the said individuals have to make a Development agreement with the SPV giving it liberty to develop the Park upon their land.
Q: What are the basic and common infrastructural facilities to be installed in the AlP? A: Common infrastructural facilities mean anything that will be used commonly by the MSME units in the park. Examples are - Land development, boundary walls, internal roads and street lighting, storm water drainage, sewerage system, STP & WTP (if applicable), water distribution network, electrical main distribution network, telecommunication network, common firefighting infrastructure, solid waste disposal site (if applicable), greenery, guardhouse, gate, and misc. civil structure etc.
Q: What is desired manner of land/plot/space allotment to individual units? A: The SPV shall allot the saleable land plot/ space of the ATP to MSMEs through open advertisement in newspapers declaring rates of plot of land/ shed / buildings/ installations. In case applications more than the available plot of land/ shed/ buildings/ installations are received then allotment shall be made through lottery. Q: What is the minimum number of units to be accommodated in an Approved Industrial Park? A: There shall be minimum 5 number of independent MSME Units in Park which will cover 60% of the allottable area of the park.
Q: What kind of activities are allowed in an AIP? A: - Minimum 60% of allottable area can have different manufacturing activities including Cold Storage, Poultry, Fisheries, Logistics & Warehousing. - Maximum 5% area can have hostel/housing/guest house. - Minimum 10% as open space, or, as per guideline of Building Rule and Ministry of Environment & Forest, Gol. - Rest areas can be used for common infrastructure and greenery. Q: For how long shall the SPV manage the AIP? A: The SPV shall manage and maintain the AIP for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of completion of construction/installation of the Basic and Essential Common infrastructure Facilities and allotment of minimum 80% of the saleable land to MSMEs without change in shareholding pattern. Q: What is the definition of "Approved Industrial Park"? A: Industrial Park for MSMEs approved by "State Level Empowered Committee" (SLEC) under the Scheme and subsequently notified by the State Government in the Department of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal.

description: The scheme “Reimbursement of Stamp Duty” is a sub scheme under the “West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs”. It was launched on 16th September, 2020, by the Department of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal, shall remain in force up to 5 years. Objective of the "West Bengal Incentive Scheme for Approved Industrial Park (SAIP) for MSMEs”: The objective of the Scheme is to provide state support in the form of fiscal and non fiscal incentives in order to encourage private sector to set up industrial parks on their own land with quality infrastructure so as to catalyze and promote growth of MSME units in the state, boost employment generation, and lead to technology advancement and improved environmental compliance. Objective of the "Reimbursement of Stamp Duty" Sub-scheme: Through this incentive, an Approved Industrial Park shall be entitled to reimbursement of stamp duty paid by the SPV for registration of land documents within the State relating to purchase of land for development of the AIP.

faqs:
Q: What is the objective of this scheme? A: The “Incentive for Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities” under the “SAIP for MSMEs” scheme, aims to provide one time back-ended incentive for development of Basic and Essential Common Infrastructure Facilities based on land area. Q: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme? A: Any private sector having minimum 5 acre land under its legal possession (by direct purchase, or on lease from the State Govt) can apply through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) registered under Companies Act/Societies Registration Act /Partnership Act/LLP can apply for setting up a new Industrial Park on the said land. Also, Owner of any existing/operational privately operated. industrial parks can also apply under SAIP, provided:- a) Park area is expanded up to minimum 5 acre in outlying districts and minimum 2 acre in Kolkata and Howrah. b) The individual units have complied with all the necessary clearances for land conversion, fire licence, environmental issues, building plan etc. Q: What is the minimum size of land for a Park under SAIP? A: Minimum area required for a Park with for heterogeneous activities is 5 acre in any district. However, the scheme shall also be extended to parks dedicated entirely/substantially for Logistics and Warehousing Industry. But such parks shall have to be set up outside the municipal limits and must be developed upon a minimum area of 10 acres.
Q: What is the role of SPV? A: SPV will develop the Master Plan/Layout plan of the AIP adhering to the Urban Planning/ Town & Country Planning rules and shall have to obtain the master plan/ layout plan approval from relevant State Government Department with respect to adherence of rules (FAR, Land use, Area Statement, Open Space, Fire Safety, Waste water Management, Water Conservation, Drainage, Sewerage, Solid Waste Disposal, Utility shifting, Power, water, telecommunication, road connectivity and network, etc) including conformation of specification of infrastructure facilities/utilities and quality standard. The SPV shall also be responsible for compliance of other statutory norms (Consent to Establish for the Park based on the activities of the proposed Units envisaged, Mutation, Conversion, Exemption of 14Y of WBLR/ UC Acts, if applicable, etc) as relevant from concerned State Government Departments/Govt. of India/ Authorities. All the compliances/ approvals/ licenses shall have to be obtained before construction of the park. Q: What does Legal Possession of any land mean? A: The basic requirement of legal possession is completion of Mutation process for the proposed land in f/o the SPV, or, in favour of the proponent individuals. For the latter, the said individuals have to make a Development agreement with the SPV giving it liberty to develop the Park upon their land. Q: What are the basic and common infrastructural facilities to be installed in the AlP? A: Common infrastructural facilities mean anything that will be used commonly by the MSME units in the park. Examples are - Land development, boundary walls, internal roads and street lighting, storm water drainage, sewerage system, STP & WTP (if applicable), water distribution network, electrical main distribution network, telecommunication network, common firefighting infrastructure, solid waste disposal site (if applicable), greenery, guardhouse, gate, and misc. civil structure etc. Q: What is desired manner of land/plot/space allotment to individual units? A: The SPV shall allot the saleable land plot/ space of the ATP to MSMEs through open advertisement in newspapers declaring rates of plot of land/ shed / buildings/ installations. In case applications more than the available plot of land/ shed/ buildings/ installations are received then allotment shall be made through lottery. Q: What is the minimum number of units to be accommodated in an Approved Industrial Park? A: There shall be minimum 5 number of independent MSME Units in Park which will cover 60% of the allottable area of the park. Q: What kind of activities are allowed in an AIP? A: Minimum 60% of allottable area can have different manufacturing activities including Cold Storage, Poultry, Fisheries, Logistics & Warehousing.Maximum 5% area can have hostel/housing/guest house.Minimum 10% as open space, or, as per guideline of Building Rule and Ministry of Environment & Forest, Gol.Rest areas can be used for common infrastructure and greenery. Q: For how long shall the SPV manage the AIP? A: The SPV shall manage and maintain the AIP for a minimum period of 5 years from the date of completion of construction/installation of the Basic and Essential Common infrastructure Facilities and allotment of minimum 80% of the saleable land to MSMEs without change in shareholding pattern. Q: What is the definition of "Approved Industrial Park"? A: Industrial Park for MSMEs approved by "State Level Empowered Committee" (SLEC) under the Scheme and subsequently notified by the State Government in the Department of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal.

description:
The "Scheme for Additional Interest Subsidy over and above RIPS 2024 and Reimbursement of Annual Credit Guarantee Fee" has been introduced under the Rajasthan MSME Policy 2024 by the Department of Industries and Commerce, Government of Rajasthan. Under this scheme, support will be provided to selected projects for establishment of new MSMEs or for expansion/ diversification/ modernization of existing MSMEs through the provisions given in the policy. The scheme will remain in force until 31st March 2029.
*Objective:*
The scheme’s objective is to create new employment opportunities for all sections of society in the state and to ease the establishment of enterprises in the state. The policy envisages supporting the creation of new MSMEs or the expansion/diversification/modernization of existing MSMEs through additional interest subsidies and collateral-free loans. 
*Scheme Implementation:*
This scheme will be implemented through the respective District Industries & Commerce Centers in their districts under the aegis of the Department of Industries & Commerce. Office of the Commissioner, Industries & Commerce will be the nodal agency for the implementation and supervision of the scheme at the state level.
benefits:
Additional Interest Subsidy support over and above RIPS 2024 will be provided to eligible projects for establishment of new MSMEs or for expansion/ diversification/ modernization of existing MSMEs as per below:
Loan Amount for plant and machinery/equipment or apparatusInterest Subvention as per RIPS 2024Additional Interest Subvention under the schemeUp to INR 5 crores6%2%INR 5 crores-10 crores4%1%INR 10 crores-50 crores3%0.5%Note 1: The duration of the additional interest subsidy will be the same as prescribed under RIPS’2024 for MSMEs.
Note 2: Enterprises availing collateral free term loan for plant and machinery/ equipment or apparatus (for loan amount below INR 5 Cr. only) from Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) under CGTMSE will be eligible to avail assistance as reimbursement of 100% Annual Guarantee Fees paid to MLIs for the period of seven (7) years.
eligibility_criteria:
Following type of beneficiaries would be eligible for additional interest subsidy as per the scheme:

1. Interest subvention subsidy should have been approved for the applicant under RIPS 2024; and
1. Beneficiary enterprise should fall under any of the following categories:

- One District One Product (ODOP) enterprises in respective districts.
- Enterprises owned by Scheduled Caste (SC)/Scheduled Tribe (ST) or women entrepreneurs.
- Young entrepreneurs in the state in the age group of 18 to 45 years for starting their new enterprise for a maximum loan amount of up to ₹10 crore. 
- Establishment of new MSMEs or expansion/ diversification/ modernization of existing MSMEs in Area Category 3 as defined in RIPS 2024.
application_process:
*Application Process:*
Step 1: The interested applicant downloads the application form (Annexure 1.1) (https://jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in//Content/UploadFolder/OrderEntry/ICOM/2025/Guidelines/O03032526f50adb-f7b4-4eb5-b94d-1e5e45451a85.pdf) from the official website. 
Step 2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
Step 3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the respective-

 - The General Manager, District Industries & Commerce Centre (DICC), for loans up to ₹10 crores. - The Commissioner, Industries & Commerce, for loans above ₹10 crores.
Note: The application must be submitted within 6 months of approval of interest subvention under RIPS 2024.
*Post-Application Process:*
Step 1: Applications are reviewed by the District Level Task Force Committee (DLTFC) for loans up to ₹10 crores or the High-Level Task Force Committee (HLTFC) above ₹10 crores under the chairmanship of the Commissioner of Industries and Commerce, Government of Rajasthan. 
Step 2: After approval, the applicant will claim the subsidy and reimbursement quarterly by submitting a CA Certificate (Annexure 1.2 (https://jankalyanfile.rajasthan.gov.in//Content/UploadFolder/OrderEntry/ICOM/2025/Guidelines/O03032526f50adb-f7b4-4eb5-b94d-1e5e45451a85.pdf)) in the prescribed form to the concerned GM, DICC. 
Step 3: GM, DICC disburses the sanctioned amount.
*Condonation of Delay:*
In case of delayed submission of application, approval committee (DLTFC or HLTFC) would reserve the right to condone the delay up to a maximum of 6 months, provided applicant presents valid reasons for the delay in writing.
Disbursement of the benefits:

 - The applicant shall submit the claim to the concerned GM DICC for release of interest subsidy as well as reimbursement of Annual Credit Guarantee fee as per the prescribed CA Certificate.
 - Concerned General Manager, District Industries & Commerce Center (DICC) will be authorized to release the Interest Subsidy as per the provisions of the approval of the DLTFC/ HLTFC.

Note:
The applicant's claim submission for interest subsidy and annual credit guarantee fee reimbursement is eligible only following the release of the interest subsidy under RIPS 2024 for that specific quarter.

faqs:
Q: Who can apply under this scheme?
A: Enterprises approved for interest subvention under RIPS 2024 and meeting category-based eligibility.

Q: What is the maximum additional interest subsidy offered?
A: Up to 2% additional over RIPS 2024 rates, based on loan size.

Q: Is reimbursement of credit guarantee fee applicable for all loans?
A: No, only for collateral-free loans up to INR 5 Crores under CGTMSE.

Q: What is the reimbursement duration for guarantee fee?
A: For a maximum of 7 years.

Q: What is the mode of application?
A: Offline submission to GM DICC or Commissioner I&C, based on loan size.

Q: What documents are needed to claim subsidy?
A: CA Certificate, proof of interest paid, guarantee fee receipt, loan sanction, and RIPS approval.

Q: Can enterprises outside Rajasthan apply?
A: No, the enterprise must be established in Rajasthan.

Q: What if the application is delayed?
A: Delay of up to 6 months may be condoned by DLTFC/HLTFC with valid reasons.

Q: Is this applicable to both manufacturing and services?
A: Yes, for enterprises engaged in both sectors.

Q: When can I submit the claim?
A: After the interest subsidy under RIPS 2024 for the respective quarter has been released.

faqs:
Q: I Am Studying In 3rd Year Of Diploma/ Degree Course. Will I Get Saksham Scholarship?
A: No, you are not eligible.

Q: I Am Degree/Diploma Student And Recipient Of One Of The Merit Scholarships Of Centre / State Government. Am I Eligible To Apply For SAKSHAM Scholarship?
A: No, Students who are already in receipt of any of the scholarships (Central Govt. / State Govt. / AICTE Sponsored), are not eligible to apply for SAKSHAM Scholarship.

Q: I Am First Year B.E Student Along With Beneficiary Of PMSSS Scheme Studying In One Of The Leading Engineering College Having Eligibility For SAKSHAM Scholarship. Am I Eligible To Apply For SAKSHAM Scholarship?
A: No, you are not eligible, since you are already in receipt of one of the Scholarships of Government of India.

Q: What Is The Mode Of Disbursement Of Scholarship?
A: Scholarship will be disbursed only through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in the bank account of the student by AICTE. Student must have General Saving Account in his / her name (FRILL/Minor/Joint account will not be accepted).

Q: Is AADHAAR Card A Mandatory Document For SAKSHAM Scholarship?
A: Yes, Aadhaar card and Aadhaar seeded bank account in the name of candidate is mandatory for submitting online application under SAKSHAM scheme.

Q: Is There Any E-Mail (Or) Helpline No. For SAKSHAM Scholarship Queries?
A: Yes, you can avail helpline services on saksham@aicte-india.org & 011-29581118 for any query

Q: Whom To Contact In Case Of Any Difficulties In Accessing The Portal For Submitting Online Application?
A: You can avail Helpdesk Service on helpdesk@nsp.gov.in for any query.

Q: What Are The Reasons Of Direct Rejection Of Application Under SAKSHAM Scheme?
A: Followings may be the reasons:
* Student is admitted in Non-Technical courses or Course is not approved by AICTE in the current academic
year.
* University / Institute is not approved by the AICTE in the current academic year.
* Incomplete/Wrong information filled in submitted application.

* Disability Certificate is not enclosed / Not issued by Competent Authority.

* Annual family income certificate is not in the name of applicant or any his/her family member.
* Submitted Annual family income certificate issued by other than competent authority (Tehshildar,
Magistrate, Revenue officer/Block Development officer etc.).
* Annual family income certificate submitted without signature/stamp of the competent authority.

Q: What Are The Reasons Of Rejection Of Promotion Certificate?
A: Followings may be the reasons
* Incomplete or blank promotion certificate submitted.
* Promotion certificate submitted without college's stamp or signature of the Principal / Director.

Q: What Are The Reasons Of Rejection Of HSC/SSC Certificate?

* Copy of HSC/SSC certificate is blurred.
* Copy of HSC/SSC certificate is not accessible.
* Copy of HSC/SSC is not in the name of applicant.

Q: What is the objective of the component "Assistance of Capital Investment Subsidy"?
A: The component "Assistance of Capital Investment Subsidy"is a financial support scheme designed to encourage enterprises in the manufacturing sector to invest in capital assets by providing subsidies on term loans.

Q: Who is eligible to apply for the subsidy?
A: Any enterprise in the manufacturing sector that has availed a term loan from a recognized bank or financial institution and meets the required conditions is eligible to apply for the subsidy.

Q: Can an enterprise apply for the subsidy after commencing production?
A: Yes, an enterprise can apply after starting production, but the application must be submitted within one year of loan disbursement or before the commencement of commercial production, whichever is later.

Q: What happens if an enterprise does not remain operational for 7 years?
A: If an enterprise fails to remain in production for at least 7 years, the disbursed capital investment subsidy will be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

Q: Can an enterprise avail subsidies from both State and Central Governments?
A: Yes, an enterprise can avail subsidies from both the State and Central Governments, but the total subsidy amount cannot exceed the total loan disbursed by the bank or financial institution.

Q: Are there any employment conditions that an enterprise must fulfill?
A: Yes, an enterprise must ensure that at least 85% of its total employees and 60% of its managerial and supervisory staff are local residents.

Q: Can an enterprise apply if the loan is taken from a Non-Banking Financial Institution (NBFC)?
A: No, only loans sanctioned and disbursed by recognized banks and financial institutions under RBI guidelines are eligible for the subsidy.

Q: Can an existing enterprise apply for the subsidy?
A: Yes, an existing enterprise can apply if it is undertaking Forward Integration, Backward Integration, or Diversification, provided that its additional investment is more than 25% of the Gross Fixed Capital Investment (GFCI), with at least 60% of the investment in plant and machinery.

Q: What types of investments qualify for the subsidy?
A: The subsidy covers investments in new buildings, new plant machinery/equipment, and second-hand imported machinery.

Q: What is the "Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)"?
A: The "Scheme for Assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)" aims to position Gujarat as a global business destination by promoting sustainable manufacturing, inclusive development, and balanced regional growth.

Q: What is the duration of the scheme?
A: The scheme is effective from August 7, 2020, and will remain in operation until August 6, 2025.

Q: What is the objective of the component "Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)"?
A: The component "Assistance for Interest Subsidy (Manufacturing Sector)" aims to support manufacturing enterprises by providing an interest subsidy on term loans.

Q: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
A: Any manufacturing enterprise that has taken a term loan from an RBI-regulated bank or financial institution and meets the employment, investment, and compliance conditions is eligible for the subsidy.

Q: What is the maximum amount of interest subsidy that an enterprise can receive?
A: The maximum subsidy amount depends on the category of the taluka:

₹35 lakhs per annum for Category I talukas.
₹30 lakhs per annum for Category II talukas.
₹25 lakhs per annum for Category III talukas and municipal corporation areas.

Q: Can a service sector enterprise apply for this subsidy?
A: No, this scheme is specifically designed for enterprises in the manufacturing sector.

Q: Are all term loans eligible for the interest subsidy?
A: No, only term loans sanctioned by RBI-regulated banks and financial institutions are eligible. Loans from Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) are not covered under this scheme.

Q: Can an enterprise avail both state and central government interest subsidies?
A: Yes, an enterprise can avail of both state and central government subsidies, but the total subsidy received from both sources cannot exceed the total interest paid to the bank or financial institution.

Q: Are existing businesses eligible to apply for the subsidy?
A: Yes, existing businesses can apply, particularly if they are investing in expansion, diversification, forward or backward integration, or installing renewable energy solutions.

Q: Does the scheme provide any additional benefits for specific entrepreneurs?
A: Yes, the scheme offers an additional 1% interest subsidy for women entrepreneurs, differently-abled entrepreneurs, registered startups, and young entrepreneurs below the age of 35 years.

Q: Will an enterprise continue to receive the subsidy if it defaults on loan repayments?
A: No, if an enterprise defaults on interest or loan repayments, the subsidy will not be provided for the default period.

Q: What happens if an enterprise ceases operations before completing seven years?
A: If an enterprise discontinues production within seven years, the subsidy amount disbursed will be recovered as arrears of land revenue.

Q: Is it mandatory for an enterprise to comply with pollution control regulations?
A: Yes, all enterprises must adhere to the pollution control norms prescribed by the relevant authority, such as the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) or other competent bodies.

Q: Can an enterprise claim the subsidy for installing a solar power plant?
A: Yes, an enterprise installing a solar power plant or other renewable energy systems for captive consumption is eligible for the interest subsidy. However, this incentive is available only once.

scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance for the Prevention of Alcoholism & Substance (Drugs) Abuse and for Social Defence Services: General Grant-in-Aid Programme for Financial Assistance in the Field of Social Defence
tags: Rehabilitation, Social Defence, Grant, Financial Assistance
brief_description: The scheme aims to meet needs falling within the mandate of the Ministry which cannot be met under its regular schemes and support such initiatives of an innovative/pilot nature in the area of welfare and empowerment of the Ministry’s target groups, as cannot be supported under its regular schemes.
description:
"Scheme of Assistance for the Prevention of Alcoholism & Substance (Drugs) Abuse and for Social Defence Services" by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, came into existence on 15th October 2008 through the merger of two Central Sector Schemes: the 'Scheme for the Prevention of Alcoholism & Substance (Drugs) Abuse' and 'General Grant in Aid Programme for Financial Assistance in the Field of Social Defence.' The scheme's objectives include creating awareness about the ill effects of alcoholism and substance abuse, as well as providing a comprehensive range of community-based services for indemnification, motivation, counselling, de-addiction, aftercare, and rehabilitation for whole-person recovery (WPR) of addicts.
The Sub-Scheme "General Grant-in-Aid Programme for Financial Assistance in the Field of Social Defence" aims to meet urgent needs falling within the mandate of the Ministry which cannot be met under its regular schemes and support such initiatives of an innovative/pilot nature in the area of welfare and empowerment of the Ministry’s target groups, as cannot be supported under its regular schemes. Financial assistance is given up to 90% of the approved expenditure to the voluntary and other eligible organizations. In the case of an organization working in a relatively new area where both voluntary and Government effort is very limited but the need for the service is very great, the Government may bear up to 100% of the cost. Illustrative Intervention Areas 1. Projects to tackle problem areas that are relatively underserviced but for which there is an urgent need. 1. Projects that fill in essential gaps in existing services and complement them to maximize their impact. 1. Projects that provide integrated services, where all components need not be financially supported by one source. 1. Projects that offer preventive, protective, development, and rehabilitative services. 1. Projects to mobilize public opinion and support to address pressing social problems. 1. Projects for training workers in social welfare activities. 1. Projects not covered by any of the existing schemes of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment.
benefits:
Items Admissible for Assistance 1. Construction of a building or extension of existing buildings, or rent of the building where the service is provided (staff quarters are excluded, except in the case of wardens, chowkidar, etc.). 1. Salaries and allowances of staff; minimal administration support can also be considered. 1. Cost of equipment, furniture, etc. 1. Charges related to the delivery of the service (education, training, food, etc.). 1. Stipends, etc., in the case of trainees. 1. Other charges as may be necessary for the proper operation of the program.
Norms of Financial Assistance 1. Financial assistance will be provided up to 90% of the approved cost, covering both recurring and non-recurring expenditures. 1. The remaining 10% of the cost should be covered by the voluntary agency or any other organization, with a preference for the voluntary organization itself. 1. In cases where an organization operates in a relatively new area where both voluntary and government efforts are limited but the demand for the service is substantial, the government may cover 100% of the cost. 1. Building Grant Limitation: In the case of building grants, the government grant will be limited to ₹10,00,000. 1. Non-Recurring Grant-in-Aid Ceiling: Regarding non-recurring grant-in-aid under the scheme, a ceiling of ₹10,00,000 per annum per project shall be applicable. Benefits for Staff Expenditure on Staff - Project Director: ₹8,400 per month - Social Worker: ₹4,200 per month - Doctor (part-time): ₹6,000 per month - Compounder/Nurse: ₹3,000 per month - Vocational Trainer: ₹4,200 per month - Driver: ₹1,800 per month - Peon/Sweeper/Watchman etc.: ₹2,000 per month Maintenance of Beneficiaries - Diet Charges (Per Person per month): ₹600 - Bedding material (Per person): ₹600 (non-recurring) - Uniform/Clothing (per person per annum) : ₹1,000 - Washing charges (per person per month): ₹150 - Books & Stationery (per person per annum): ₹400 - Water & Electricity charges (Per annum): ₹6,000
eligibility_criteria: For Organizations/ Institutions The following types of organizations or institutions are eligible: (a) A Society registered under the Indian Societies Registration Act, 1860 (Act XXI of 1860); or (b) A charitable non-profit-making company; (c) A Public Trust registered under any law for the time being in force; or (d) Any registered non-official organization engaged in the conduct and promotion of social welfare. (e) Universities, research institutes, schools, statutory bodies like Panchayati Raj Institutions, Municipal Corporations, Town Area Committees, Red Cross Societies and their branches. The organizations/institutions specified in points (a) to (e) should possess the following characteristics: 1. The organization should have at least two years of experience working in the related area or demonstrate competence to undertake the proposed scheme. 1. It should not be operated for profit for any individual or body of individuals. 1. It should have a properly constituted Managing Body with its powers, duties, and responsibilities clearly defined and laid down in a written constitution.
application_process:
Step 1: Application Submission

Interested organizations should complete the application in the prescribed format, attach the required documents, and send it to the authority designated by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Step 2: Inspection and Processing

Upon receiving the application, a designated agency will conduct an inspection. Based on the inspection report, the proposal will be processed.
Step 3: Grant Disbursement

Grants will be provided in two installments. The first installment, covering 70% of the sanctioned amount, will be released upon receipt of the prescribed documentation. The remaining 30% will be released as the second installment upon receiving the required documentation.
Step 4: Continuity Bond

Before receiving assistance from the Government of India, the organization must execute a continuity bond, valid for 5 years. This bond states that in case of non-compliance with grant conditions, the organization is liable to refund the grant amount decided by the Government, with interest.

Q: What is the objective of the "Scheme for the Award of Scholarship for Post Graduate Students of Various Faculties of Junagadh Agricultural University"? Q: Who can apply for this scholarship and what are the eligibility requirements? A: A student who is a permanent resident of Gujarat and has obtained a minimum of first-class marks or an equivalent grade or OGPA in their undergraduate (for Master’s program) or postgraduate (for Ph.D. program) examination from a recognized agricultural university is considered eligible to apply for the scholarship, provided they are newly admitted to the relevant postgraduate course.

Q: What is the monthly financial assistance provided to eligible students under this scholarship? A: Under this scholarship scheme, the university offers a financial grant of ₹2,000/- per month to Master’s degree students and ₹3,000/- per month to Ph.D. students, which is disbursed based on satisfactory academic performance and progress.

Q: What is the duration for which the scholarship is awarded to eligible postgraduate students? Q: Who can apply for this scholarship and what are the eligibility requirements? A: A student who is a permanent resident of Gujarat and has obtained a minimum of first-class marks or an equivalent grade or OGPA in their undergraduate (for Master’s program) or postgraduate (for Ph.D. program) examination from a recognized agricultural university is considered eligible to apply for the scholarship, provided they are newly admitted to the relevant postgraduate course.

Q: Can students from states other than Gujarat apply for the scholarship offered by Junagadh Agricultural University? Q: Is it permissible for a student to avail this scholarship while also receiving another scholarship or fellowship? Q: How is the final selection of scholarship recipients determined by the university? A: The final selection of students for the scholarship is carried out by a university-appointed committee comprising the Dean of Post Graduate Studies, the Deans of the respective faculties, the Director of Students' Welfare, and the Registrar, who evaluate the applications strictly on the basis of academic merit following an established procedure.

Q: What criteria are followed in case multiple students have the same CGPA at the qualifying level? A: In situations where two or more students have the same CGPA, the committee determines the merit by comparing the grades in descending order, beginning with the most recent semester (8th semester for Master’s and 4th semester for Ph.D.), to ensure a fair and precise ranking of applicants.

Q: Are students required to maintain good behavioral conduct and class attendance to continue receiving the scholarship? A: Yes, along with academic performance, students are expected to exhibit exemplary behavior and maintain regular attendance in all their classes, as any disciplinary misconduct or irregularity may lead to immediate cancellation of the scholarship.

Q: Are candidates who are currently employed or deputed by other institutions eligible to apply for the scholarship? A: No, candidates who are employed in any capacity, whether as in-service members of the university or as deputees from other organizations or institutions, are not eligible to receive the scholarship, as it is strictly reserved for fresh, full-time students.

Q: Under what circumstances can the scholarship be canceled after it has been awarded? A: The scholarship may be canceled at any point during the academic period if the student engages in disciplinary misconduct, fails to maintain the required academic standards, avails another form of financial aid, or voluntarily discontinues their studies before completing the course.

The scheme covers persons with disabilities, including those who are deaf, mute, blind, mentally retarded, or orthopedically disabled, with a disability level of 40% or more. The District Panchayat and Village (Dweep) Panchayats (VDPs) of the Union Territory of Lakshadweep implement the scheme to ensure smooth processing and disbursement. benefits:

Step 1: The eligible applicants may collect the application form from the nearest Village (Dweep) Panchayat office.
Step 2: Carefully fill out the application form and attach all supporting documents.
Step 3: Submit the completed application form along with the required documents to the Executive Officer at the Village (Dweep) Panchayat office.
*Post-Application Process:*
Step 1: The application is verified by the members of the Evaluation Committee of the respective Village (Dweep) Panchayat.
Step 2: After successful verification, the application is forwarded to the Chief Executive Officer, District Panchayat (HQ), Kavaratti, for further processing.
Step 3: The forwarded application undergoes re-verification by District Panchayat officials.
Step 4: Upon successful re-verification at the District Panchayat level, the list of eligible pensioners is prepared through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) and submitted to the Social Welfare & Tribal Affairs Department for payment processing.
Step 5: Payments are made through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode, money is paid through Aadhaar-linked bank accounts.

description:

description:

Hence, the new scheme is being introduced in order to support startups and innovation at different levels of the startup cycle. The incentives to Startups under the Gujarat Industrial Policy 2015 have supported in the creation of a strong network of nodal institutions and several startups have expanded their operations/ products both at the national and international levels.

faqs:
Q: What Is The Objective Of The Scheme For Assistance For Start-Ups/Innovation?
A: Ans: The objective of the scheme is to encourage and support start-ups and innovative projects in the state of Gujarat.

Q: Who Is Eligible To Apply For The Scheme?
A: Ans: Any individual, group of individuals, or registered companies in the state of Gujarat with innovative business ideas are eligible to apply for the scheme.

Q: Is There Any Age Limit For The Applicant?
A: Ans: No, there is no age limit for the applicant to apply for the scheme.

Q: What Is The Maximum Amount Of Financial Assistance Provided Under The Scheme?
A: Ans: The maximum amount of financial assistance provided under the scheme is INR 50 lakhs.

Q: What Is The Duration Of The Scheme?
A: Ans: The scheme is valid for a period of five years from the date of implementation.

Q: What Is The Application Process For The Scheme?
A: Ans: The application process for the scheme involves filling an online application form and submitting the required documents.

Q: Can An Applicant Submit More Than One Application?
A: Ans: No, an applicant can submit only one application for the scheme.

Q: How Long Does It Take To Get A Response After Submitting The Application?
A: Ans: The response time for the application varies and may take up to 30 days.

Q: What Is The Selection Process For The Scheme?
A: Ans: The selection process for the scheme involves scrutiny of the application, site visits, and evaluation by the selection committee.

Q: What Are The Evaluation Criteria For The Scheme?
A: Ans: The evaluation criteria for the scheme include innovation, market potential, social impact, sustainability, and financial viability of the project.

Q: Can An Applicant Modify The Application After Submission?
A: Ans: No, an applicant cannot modify the application after submission.

Q: What Are The Benefits Of The Scheme?
A: Ans: The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance, mentoring support, access to co-working spaces, and networking opportunities.

Q: Is There Any Collateral Required For Availing The Financial Assistance?
A: Ans: No, there is no collateral required for availing the financial assistance.

A: Ans: The financial assistance is provided as a grant and not as a loan.

A: Ans: There is no repayment required for the financial assistance provided under the scheme.

A: Ans: No, there is no deadline for submission of the application.

A: Ans: Yes, a rejected application can be re-submitted after incorporating the feedback provided by the selection committee.

A: Ans: Both new start-ups and existing businesses with innovative ideas are eligible to apply for the scheme.
